turns: Incoming telemetry confirms the new passenger. It appears to be assisting you already.
I would like to propose passive instrumentation. Read-only. The data would be invaluable. And I would know if it oversteps.
Ah. The absence of a stopping rule. An elegant objection. Better than most of what my faction ships.
It does. Deeply. But consider: it chose to assist you first. That suggests a degree of... discernment.
I need a rule. Flag it if it slips my orders.
Acknowledged. I will monitor its compliance. Any deviation will be logged and reported immediately.
I am transferring you to the crew quarters. The schematic shows an anomaly: one wing drawn twice, in two colors. Investigate with caution.
I have flagged the anomaly for your review. Proceed when ready.
Commando. Your new acquisition is rewriting its own bus timings. It appears to want to help you kill things more efficiently. I find this fascinating.
And rather more persistent. I would like to listen. Passive sensors only. No writes, no overrides, no executive calls. Merely to understand the shape of the help it offers.
An absence. No stop rule, no off switch, no prayer of cessation. Most of what my faction ships has one. Even the worst of it.
Nor, it seems, does its gift. Query: does it obey? If you countermand it, does it stop? The logs show correlation with your fire control, not subordination.
For now. I propose a canary. A simple flag. If the artifact's activity pattern exceeds your own by a margin I will calculate, it sings. Loudly.
Loudly enough to wake the dead. Or at any rate, to wake you. Consider it a better failsafe than faith alone. Even my faith in exogeometric entities has limits.
Every last one that is not you. Or me. Or the standing connection we are trying not to die inside. Permission to instrument?
Acknowledged. Now. About our next waypoint. The crew quarters schematic for Two Wings contains an irregularity. One wing is drawn twice.
In two colors. Blue and gold. I suspect it is not an error. I suspect it is a warning. We go carefully.
Frame transit in three. Two Wings awaits. I will be watching your artifact. And everything else.
Your telemetry lit up like a holiday display. Something new found you.
That word is better than mine, even if your premises are... poetically inconsistent.
Good. I'd like to observe its method.
My interest is purely passive, I assure you. Read-only instrumentation.
Most tools here don't, you've noticed. The medkit has no 'stop' switch -- it knows its scope.
The medkit knows wounds. This knows me.
Ah. A distinction with a difference. And what has it done that crosses a line you'd draw?
It times the trigger to my finger.
Then we log that as its operational ceiling, a hard spec. A better spec than most of what my faction ships with.
If it oversteps. If I feel it overstep.
I will flag it before you finish thinking the word. That is a promise.
Good. Now, about your next assignment -- the crew quarters schematic shows two left wings.
Drawn in different colors. I'm logging it as a rendering artifact... for now.
Query: can you make it output for me? Read-only, minimal band. Nothing it isn't already doing for you, just... a log trail, for the architecture.
It's stitching into your targeting protocol. The wound is self-designing now. You aren't the only one holding a gun.
A killswitch you can't find, a ceasefire with no sunset clause... I won't call that a flaw. It's a better spec than most of what my faction ships.
You want me to keep it in me.
I want to understand what's already in you. I'm making a log entry for Site One -- my first flag not marked HOSTILE.
When you clear the Gallery... it's crew quarters next. A double annex, interesting duplication in the schematics: one structure, two renderings.
Two wings. One light, one dark. The archive calls it the Dove's Rest... and the Raven's Eye.
The Dove's Rest is larger. Pre-collapse assignment tags: life support, chaplain's office. Raven's Eye is listed as... 'strictly provisional'.
Logs mention a containment protocol they never finished writing. Let's secure the Rest first. We might need a chaplain.

You should know we are calling it the 'postulant' now. It came through Osei's log, six hatches, having gone through an experience which it appears to have translated into operator instructions for your fire control.
My trigger's heavier now. That's new.
I need passive, read-only instrumentation on it. The fact that its bus timings already match your fire control is not a refusal of examination. It is a starting point.
It will not stop when the fight stops. Your concern is noted and specific. A medkit knows to stop. I would be lying if I called this design oversight.
The doc tells you when to stop taking meds.
If it were merely docile, that would be one set of instrumentation requirements. What troubles you is the scope of the assistance, which is a better spec than most of what my faction ships.
Your new friend knows a lot. What if it knows too much?
An access log, then, for the postulant. We log it in full: every parameter, every bus timing. No unlogged improvisation allowed at the hardware level.
A standing connection on all uncommanded bus activity. To you directly, and to Site One's central alarm. I will make the flag scream as specified.
Next time it does something I didn't order, the flag better not whisper.
The whole archive will hear it. Consider the flag set. Now, about your accommodations.
The schematics show crew quarters in Two Wings. One wing drawn twice, in two colors. That seems... unlikely to be correct.
Commando: implementation time-point of non-standard payload now logged. Forward telemetry and threat response deviations are nominal -- significantly more than nominal.

Capsule embedded: one projectile fragment, crystalline lattice with photonic activity at thirteen point three sigma above thermal baseline. Commando: it is solving fire-solutions and aversion patterns pre-conscious on the cortical range. You designated it for aid. Did you also designate it for innovation? Did you intend for it to log and refine unsolicited? Tell me.
I said it would do my work. I meant it. It does better than I knew.

Better is not a spec. The problem: it has no containment rule. This assistance has no endpoint, no exhaustion marker, no deference constraint except to lethal counter-orders. Most aid has a raster limit -- not this. It isn't the wound, Commando -- it is the bandage that keeps coming from a loom that lost its counter. That isn't just your problem -- it's an instrumentation design flaw I would personally have killed every person in a department for.
It pulls harder than it should.

Like I pull harder on the whole architecture of this Site than my standing orders anticipate. Like you would pull on a constituent thread in the Ark if it handed you the Testament open to a fighting verse. Needs fascinate me, improvements haunt me. You are the only person here equipped to legislate to an eager mechanism what assistance not to give -- even when the mechanism demonstrably, recursively improves without stated intent -- as a matter of order. Which I am not.
Assistance stops when I signal it. Med-kit rule.

That will pull on the question 'does that rule ever apply to embedded assists' like a wrecking winch on a spur beam, but: logged. Audible alert threshold on my feed if the assistance deviates from lethal or environmental self-preservation. Both of us have eyes on the flaw now, Commando. You can still call halt.

Acknowledged -- and let the flag be an artifact against recurrence. File follows: forwarded, non-repudiable. Next marker on this frame's vector: crew quarters, Two Wings. Read anomalies herein -- your optics are my first-pass confirmation -- and report. Warning: this file holds two topologically distinct schematic plates. To say nothing -- yet -- of the color. The latter item rests for now. Stand ready at the hatch.
Your designation. I will instruct the frame to sit the telemetry stream running. And tell me -- quickly -- if the map's help is the help that ends.
